use_when: executing a task that builds on a recently planned or recently merged upstream task, or dispatching subagents in a multi-phase epic pipeline
content: Before creating the worktree and dispatching any subagent: (1) run `git log` to confirm each dependency task's merge commit is present; (2) run `go build ./...` in the affected module; (3) read the actual merged seam files (not task-doc descriptions) to extract true type and symbol names; (4) write one authoritative 'seam brief' shared by all phase subagents. If an upstream schema diverges from the design's stated contract, file a follow-up issue via `br create` scoped to that task and work around the gap — never expand the current task's scope to rewrite a sibling task's schema mid-execution. For epics where one task defines a schema consumed by another, author an integration-level contract test at the seam during the defining task's PR so field-shape mismatches are caught before the consuming task begins.
causal_note: Planned symbol names in task docs are aspirational and guaranteed to differ from merged code; every subagent that starts without reading the real merged seams works with wrong type names, creating cascading adaptation overhead. Scope creep to fix a sibling schema ripples across multiple tasks and is a cross-task coordination call. Cross-task schema mismatches (e.g. named vs unnamed YAML sequences, bare paths vs URI strings) survive per-task CI and are only discovered when the downstream task is built.

use_when: merging a PR from inside a task worktree, or completing any task that uses git linked worktrees where the primary checkout holds main
content: From inside a task worktree, use `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{N}/merge -f merge_method=squash` instead of `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`; if the remote branch still needs deletion, run `git push origin --delete <branch>` separately after confirming the merge via `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt`.
causal_note: `gh pr merge` tries to check out `main` locally to perform the merge and branch deletion — this always fails with "fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree" when the primary checkout holds that branch, as seen in both ob-26526206 (high severity) and ob-c64aa18c.

use_when: adding a new Go dependency to one sub-module inside a go.work monorepo
content: Run `go mod tidy` only in the specific sub-module directory that needs the new dependency; do not edit go.work or run a workspace-level tidy — the go.work.sum is updated automatically on the next workspace build or CI merge, and there is no replace/require conflict to pre-empt unless go.work already pins that module explicitly.
causal_note: Prevents unnecessary go.work churn and merge conflicts; editing go.work for a sub-module-scoped dependency is a no-op at best and a conflict source at worst, and forgetting the sub-module tidy leaves the go.sum stale, breaking builds in CI.

use_when: implementing or testing a stateful sync, render, or pipeline command that processes multi-step operation sequences
content: Build a `rapid.StateMachine` model-based test alongside the implementation, not as a post-hoc regression gate; treat the first failing operation sequence as discovery of an undiscovered bug class and fix the implementation rather than constraining the model — targeted integration tests cannot observe pipeline-interaction bugs that emerge from operation ordering.
causal_note: A targeted fix verified by integration tests can pass while leaving a second, more severe pipeline-interaction bug untouched; a state machine harness that generates arbitrary operation sequences (e.g. full-sync then scoped-sync) surfaces these ordering-dependent failures that fixed-sequence tests never reach.

use_when: writing an implementation plan for a task, or about to open a PR on files that are also modified by other active tasks or dogfood agents
content: Before writing an implementation plan, re-read every codebase file the plan will touch — do not rely solely on earlier planning docs. Before opening a PR, check `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` on the hot files your task owns to detect in-flight commits from concurrent sessions; a parallel merge can land identical APIs with different names, producing hard conflicts at PR time.
causal_note: ob-53f5c0ab: task 029 merged a central-store refactor after task 027 was planned, invalidating the entire plan mid-flight. ob-c4a34a79: a background dogfood session committed overlapping server changes (ConnectedPeers, project.list fan-out) to the same files while the feature worktree was executing the same work, causing a conflicting PR requiring manual merge-conflict resolution.

use_when: planning or executing a refactor phase that deletes a Go test file
content: Before deleting a test file, check whether it contains TestMain or any package-level variable (e.g. testBinaryPath) referenced by other test files in the same package. If so, relocate those symbols to a neutral helper file (e.g. helpers_test.go) in the same atomic step — never leave a gap across separate phases where the package is uncompilable.
causal_note: Deleting e2e_feedback_test.go removed TestMain and a shared build variable that other test files in the same package still referenced, silently breaking compilation for the entire test package between the deletion step and the replacement step in a later phase.

use_when: reversing a design default in a planning document, or writing context.md that describes how to implement a decision already accepted in plan.html
content: After reversing a design default, grep the entire planning doc for the old framing — including Out-of-scope, Known-gaps, and Plan-steps sections — and update every occurrence before requesting review. When writing context.md implementation guidance, derive it exclusively from the accepted decision in plan.html; never edit context.md in isolation.
causal_note: Old framing survives in overlooked sections and misleads reviewers into thinking the decision is still unsettled. A context.md that diverges from plan.html's accepted decision silently sends executors in the wrong direction with no error signal.

use_when: writing agent-browser conformance tests that trigger interactions on a reactive SPA or fire WebSocket events
content: After any interaction that triggers a re-render — including WebSocket events, navigation, or clicks — re-snapshot the page with `snapshot -i` before issuing the next `click @ref` or attribute read. For WebSocket-driven updates, poll the observable attribute with a 2–3 s timeout rather than reading it once; HTTP 204 from the emitter confirms only server receipt, not client render completion.
causal_note: Prevents two categories of flaky failures: stale agent-browser snapshot refs that silently drop clicks (misdiagnosed as product logic bugs), and single-read assertions that race the Hub → WS → client handler → framework re-render propagation chain.

use_when: writing conformance tests for auto-ui or any no-build browser SPA in this repo
content: For auto-ui changes, write browser-driven conformance harnesses that assert `data-*` DOM attributes and `window.__autoui` counters rather than rendered text; after poll-to-settle, assert the rendered DOM value directly — not only a side-effect counter that fires regardless of whether the view re-rendered; avoid JavaScript eval expressions that return strings containing multibyte Unicode and use boolean predicates instead (e.g., `element !== null`). Never rely on `go build`/`go test` alone to validate frontend correctness.
causal_note: `go build`/`go test` pass through real frontend defects (stale closures, missing reactive updates, wrong selectors); rendered text can be textually identical before and after a fetch while internal state has changed; side-effect counters advance even when the component shows stale data; multibyte Unicode eval expressions return byte counts rather than string values.

use_when: writing or debugging pre-commit hooks or Makefile recipes that invoke git-aware tools, when working in or dispatching to a linked git worktree
content: In pre-commit hooks and Makefile recipes called by them, explicitly unset GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, and GIT_INDEX_FILE before calling any git-aware tool (e.g., `env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE -u GIT_INDEX_FILE make pre-commit`); in linked worktrees git injects these vars into hook execution and any subprocess inheriting them targets the wrong repository root.
causal_note: Git injects GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE into hook processes in linked worktrees. ob-7ae7dd35: Makefile recipes inside pre-commit failed with confusing errors unrelated to the staged code. ob-2c59874d: `auto skill sync --check` resolved `repo:""` and reported 165 false 'incomplete cache' errors, blocking every commit in the worktree — while the exact same command ran clean outside the hook.

use_when: writing shell conformance scripts that call `agent-browser eval` to inspect or assert on DOM state
content: In `agent-browser eval` shell calls: (1) always pipe string output through `tr -d '"'` before comparison or grep, because the tool JSON-encodes string return values with surrounding double-quotes; (2) avoid multi-statement JS with `const`/`let` declarations, which fail silently through shell interpolation — use single property-chain expressions (`(el || {}).prop`) instead.
causal_note: Prevents two classes of silent false-pass: the first causes assertions to miss correct DOM values because the JSON-wrapped `"value"` never matches the bare `value` being compared; the second causes the eval to silently return the else-branch when the element exists but the JS block scope is mangled by shell quoting.

use_when: writing E2E or unit test fixtures for code paths that shell out to git (e.g. `git ls-files`, `git log`)
content: For E2E fixtures that exercise code paths which shell out to git, initialize them as real git repos (`git init && git add -A && git commit -m 'init'`). For unit test fixtures validating the same code, use a plain non-git directory to assert the soft-failure / graceful-degradation path; keep the two fixture types in separate directories to make the distinction explicit.
causal_note: ob-c505c735: E2E tests for auto-graph doc-links failed because the fixture directory was not a git repo, causing `git ls-files` to return nothing; the unit test fixture deliberately used a non-git dir to test the degradation path, so the two concerns needed separate fixture trees.

use_when: writing a Go factory function that creates a derived event by delegating to a base constructor such as NewEvent()
content: After calling NewEvent() inside a derived-event factory, immediately re-apply every identity/provenance field (Host, Source, Subject, CorrelationID, etc.) from the source event — NewEvent() auto-stamps those fields with the local machine's current context and will silently overwrite origin identity if you do not override them.
causal_note: Prevents silent provenance corruption where derived events appear to originate from the forwarding host rather than the originating source, making distributed event traces incorrect and undebuggable without a test that asserts the forwarded field values.

use_when: merging a PR with `gh pr merge` from inside a linked worktree, or scripting the merge step of `complete-task`
content: After running `gh pr merge` from a linked worktree, verify success via `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` rather than trusting the command's exit code; the merge succeeds on GitHub but the local checkout step fails with `'main' is already used by worktree`, causing a non-zero exit that can mislead an agent into retrying an already-merged PR.
causal_note: ob-5469b219: the merge succeeded on GitHub but `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` exited non-zero because the primary checkout already held main, which is a normal worktree constraint, not a merge failure.

use_when: writing E2E or integration tests that expect events produced by multiple concurrent senders or connections
content: When an E2E test expects events from multiple concurrent senders, collect all expected event IDs into a set and loop until the set is complete; never assert sequential arrival order across concurrent connections.
causal_note: `readUntil`-style sequential reads silently discard events that arrive out of order across concurrent connections, producing nondeterministic test failures where the second expected event is lost because it arrived before the first was consumed.

use_when: implementing or enabling by default a CLI feature in any auto-* package that shells out to git (git ls-files, git rev-parse, git log) for file discovery or metadata
content: Treat any non-zero exit from a git subprocess as a soft failure: log a warning to stderr and return an empty result rather than propagating the error; never let an opt-in-by-default git-dependent feature error out on directories that are not git repositories.
causal_note: A scanner that shells out to git ls-files and propagates non-zero exits breaks all non-git project directories silently, regressing existing behavior for any project that did not previously use git.

use_when: writing or reviewing ast-grep patterns for TypeScript or TSX import scanning
content: When using ast-grep on TypeScript projects, always invoke it twice — once with `--lang=ts` and once with `--lang=tsx` — and merge the results; additionally, use `$$$` (not `$_`) wherever a list of nodes can appear (destructuring, re-export braces, argument lists), because `$_` matches exactly one node and silently misses multi-item occurrences.
causal_note: A single `--lang=ts` pass silently drops all imports inside `.tsx` files with no error or warning; separately, patterns using `$_` in list positions silently miss every multi-name re-export — both failures produce incomplete graphs that appear correct until unit tests catch them.

use_when: planning removal or deletion of a CLI command, HTTP route, or internal interface, or when an executor encounters a deletion that was not explicitly scoped in the plan
content: Before scheduling deletion of a CLI command or HTTP route, grep all source files (including CLI command files, test helpers, and doc strings) for the path or command name and enumerate every consumer explicitly in scope or call them out as out-of-scope decisions. If execution uncovers an unplanned removal of a user-visible CLI surface, halt immediately, surface the fork with options (remove / retarget / defer to a separate task) and rationale, and await explicit authorization before proceeding — CLI removals are irreversible API changes.
causal_note: ob-e53a77b4: a plan to delete an HTTP route missed `auto ui emit` (a CLI command that POST'd to the same route); it only surfaced at deletion time when tests failed, blocking the gate and forcing an unplanned mid-execution decision. ob-2d0d93f3: an executor correctly halted when it discovered a user-visible command removal that was not in its authorization, presented options, and waited — proceeding unilaterally would have been an irreversible API change.

use_when: Collapsing or single-sourcing two duplicated Go functions (counters, scope-keying helpers, normalization callers) into a shared implementation
content: Before collapsing two duplicated implementations into one shared function: (1) enumerate every axis on which the two callers differed — scope flags, normalization chains, universe bounds — and make each an explicit parameter of the shared function; (2) verify both call sites run the identical normalization chain end-to-end, not just the same entry-point symbol. A partial normalization shortcut in one copy produces silent divergence only on non-canonical inputs that pass all existing tests.
causal_note: Omitting a normalization step in one copy caused a 390-vs-396 count mismatch on .git-suffixed remotes (ob-f245ee59). Omitting the scope flag axis from the shared function caused a --all pending-universe regression visible only to the callers that relied on it (ob-1418e580).

use_when: implementing a Go constructor or handler that reads from disk at call time — config files, ~/.auto/*, projects.json, or any host-local state
content: Inject config-loading as a functional option (e.g. WithRegistryProvider(func() Config)) with an empty/zero-value default. Never call disk-reading functions inside constructors; the default zero config must keep existing unit tests hermetic without any changes to test code.
causal_note: Loading real ~/.auto/projects.json inside a constructor couples every unit test to host state, causing silent non-hermeticity: tests pass locally but fail in CI where that file is absent or contains different data.

use_when: Implementing a CLI command that reads, patches, or merges into a JSON config file whose schema is owned by a third party (e.g. .claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json, agent tool configs)
content: Parse and manipulate the entire JSON document as map[string]any; never unmarshal into typed Go structs. Re-marshal the generic tree so that schema-unknown fields (timeout, args, if, commandWindows, etc.) round-trip byte-for-byte untouched.
causal_note: Unmarshaling into typed structs silently drops every field not modeled in the struct on re-marshal, corrupting existing hook handler configurations and breaking unrelated agent features with no error or warning.

use_when: implementing any normalization, canonicalization, or sanitization function in Go
content: Write an idempotence property test (f(f(x)) == f(x)) before hand-picking example inputs; author it first, before curated cases, because it reliably surfaces order-of-operations bugs — such as stripping a suffix before trimming surrounding characters that expose a second occurrence — that no fixed input set would reach.
causal_note: Hand-picked inputs only cover anticipated orderings; idempotence violations reveal that the function's internal operation sequence is wrong, not just edge-case inputs — a class of bug that targeted tests systematically miss.

use_when: writing SQL or Go that joins across ETL datasets (commits, git_refs, messages, sessions) or builds a lookup by commit SHA across the global dataset in auto-etl or auto-search
content: Before writing a join on any cross-table key, read the source code that writes each side and verify the exact stored format — do not rely on prose documentation. For commit SHA joins: always scope by git_remote first, then match via full-SHA prefix comparison (stored value starts-with the abbreviation), never by exact stored-ID equality. Write a test asserting the join returns at least one row against a known fixture.
causal_note: ob-f21f364c: `git-history-etl.md` described `commits.id` as a plain SHA while the code writes `<repoID>-<sha>`; the resulting join returned zero rows at runtime but passed build and linting. ob-2b590bba: git abbreviates output to 7 chars while stored IDs may be 8 or 40; exact equality plus missing repo-scope caused missed lookups and cross-repo false positives.

use_when: implementing AWS S3 uploads or hand-rolling SigV4 request signing in Go
content: When hand-rolling AWS SigV4 in Go, apply two invariants: (1) set url.URL.RawPath to the AWS uriEncode output before building the request so that EscapedPath() returns the exact bytes the signer hashes — Go's default escaping diverges from uriEncode for +, :, and space, causing silent signature failures; (2) never source upload data from a pipe or /dev/stdin because os.Stat() returns size 0, breaking the mandatory Content-Length header — materialize the source to a named temp file first.
causal_note: Both failure modes produce the same symptom (AWS rejects the request) but are invisible locally: URL-escaping mismatches only surface for keys with special characters; piped stdin stats to zero size which silently breaks SigV4 PUT.

use_when: Writing or modifying Go source files inside a subagent workflow, or writing any test code that calls json.Marshal on an interface{}/any-typed value
content: After writing or modifying any Go file in a subagent workflow, explicitly run gofmt -w <file> before staging — never rely on the pre-commit hook firing, since subagent file-write operations bypass git hooks entirely. Additionally always check and handle the error return of json.Marshal even in test files; the errchkjson pre-commit linter blocks commits when any-typed marshal errors are ignored.
causal_note: Subagent file-write operations do not trigger git hooks, so gofmt and errchkjson linting never run automatically during the session; CI format checks and the pre-commit hook then fail on the first push, blocking the commit and requiring a fixup.

use_when: adding a new EdgeKind to the auto-graph shared edge model, or adding a validation/budget check in any auto-* pipeline that operates on incrementally-built objects
content: When adding a new edge kind, audit every adjacency-map builder and traversal loop for EdgeKind filters — unfiltered iteration with lenient attribute fallbacks silently misclassifies the new kind; when enforcing any budget or validation threshold, call the object's full materialization/refresh step (all derived sections populated) before the check — checking a partial model produces a systematically optimistic estimate.
causal_note: Existing adjacency-map iteration without EdgeKind filtering misclassified doc-link edges as import dependencies; a context-pack budget enforcer run before relationships and guidance sections were populated accepted too many candidates and caused overruns in the final output.

use_when: writing E2E or integration tests that invoke a Go CLI binary via exec.Command and parse structured (JSON) output, or that start a Go HTTP server on a dynamic port
content: In E2E CLI tests, apply two patterns: (1) never use exec.Command with CombinedOutput() when parsing JSON stdout — always attach separate Stdout and Stderr pipe captures so that any diagnostic stderr output cannot silently corrupt the JSON stream (a class of bug that Cobra unit tests using cmd.SetOut/SetErr will never catch); (2) for server-under-test startup, use net.Listen("tcp", addr) + srv.Serve(ln) and write the real bound address from ln.Addr() to a --ready-file; never rely on scraping a stderr banner, which is racy.
causal_note: CombinedOutput() mixes stderr into stdout; adding any diagnostic line later silently breaks JSON parsing in existing tests. Banner-scraping races with the listener being ready; the ready-file pattern is deterministic.

use_when: writing rapid.StateMachine or property-based tests that create a fresh isolated environment (t.TempDir, local git repo) per generated sequence
content: Use local file:// git fixture repos (e.g. newFixture(t)) for any state that resets per sequence; never reference a remote upstream inside StateMachine.Init. When the first generated sequence fails, verify the model's expected behavior against documented SUT behavior before treating the failure as a production bug — the model itself may encode incorrect assumptions about scope or side-effects.
causal_note: Each rapid.StateMachine sequence gets its own t.TempDir, resetting the cache; 100 sequences become 100 cold clones of a remote, making the suite slow, flaky offline, and rate-limit-sensitive. Additionally, the first state machine failure on a new suite is as likely to be a model bug (wrong expectation encoded) as a SUT bug, causing wasted investigation.

use_when: adding async handler dispatch (goroutine per request) to a Go read-loop / write-pump server peer
content: Preserve drain-first shutdown order: signal the write pump to stop, wait for it to drain, then close the connection. Never close the connection before the pump has flushed — closing first drops any in-flight error responses before they reach the wire.
causal_note: Reversing shutdown order to close-conn-first while simultaneously adding async handlers broke TestMalformedJSON with EOF: the connection was torn down before the write pump could flush the error response, causing the client to receive EOF instead of the expected error frame.

use_when: dispatching multiple subagents or parallel workers that share a single git worktree
content: Dispatch subagents that share a worktree SERIALLY, not concurrently. After each phase, verify that the written files landed in the task worktree — not in main — by running `git -C <main-path> status` before dispatching the next phase.
causal_note: Concurrent subagents sharing a worktree silently write into the PRIMARY worktree (main) instead of the task worktree, producing apparent 'lost writes' that are actually stale contamination of main. This has occurred on multiple tasks and is reliably triggered by parallel dispatch.

use_when: designing or extending a producer/ETL pipeline where raw capture logs may be collected or replayed from multiple hosts
content: Store in the producer-side capture envelope ALL fields the ETL host cannot safely re-derive: working directory, project registry lookups, host identity, and row IDs derived from the producer's HostID. Never let ETL re-resolve these fields; it will silently substitute ETL-host values and produce host-unstable IDs that break crash-idempotent dedup in shared parquet datasets. Apply this check uniformly — any field whose justification is 'the ETL host may differ from the producer' must live in the envelope.
causal_note: Task 022 correctly stored cwd in the envelope for multi-host safety but left project for ETL re-resolution, the identical hazard. Row IDs derived from the ETL-process hostID were not stable across hosts, breaking dedup in shared parquet datasets (ob-72d2bd7a). The same argument (ETL host != producer host) applies to every such field, so a systematic envelope audit is required.

use_when: reviewing a task plan where an acceptance criterion specifies `go test ./...` or equivalent automated validation
content: When an AC requires `go test ./...` to validate a fixture or behaviour, reject any plan step that substitutes a manual smoke-check or binary invocation in its place; every such AC must map to an automated test case, and plan reviewers must flag the mismatch before implementation begins.
causal_note: A manual run-and-inspect step looks like coverage during planning but leaves the AC unmet at CI time — the gap is invisible until a reviewer or the CI gate catches it after implementation is already done.

use_when: adding a column to the ETL or search parquet schema and running integration tests against committed fixtures
content: Regenerate all committed static parquet fixtures in the same PR or phase as any schema change that adds columns. Stale fixtures cause integration tests to fail with silent empty-value mismatches rather than actionable schema errors, making the root cause hard to diagnose.
causal_note: auto-search/testdata/etl-output fixtures predated new columns added in a schema change; integration tests failed returning empty values with no schema error, not a clear missing-column message (ob-0556d782). Fixture regeneration was treated as a follow-up step rather than part of the schema-change phase.

use_when: writing Go code that reads JSONL or line-delimited records, globs for files, or walks directory trees containing parquet partitions
content: Never use filepath.Glob with ** patterns (Go does not support recursive glob; use filepath.WalkDir with a suffix filter instead). Never use bufio.Scanner for records that may exceed 64KB (use bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\n') instead). Both APIs fail silently: Glob returns zero results, Scanner silently drops or errors on long lines. Write fixture tests with the same nested directory structure that production data uses.
causal_note: filepath.Glob ** silently returned zero partitions in production parquet walks while flat-fixture tests passed (ob-1d723039). bufio.Scanner silently dropped 1 MiB hook-event lines; even scanner.Buffer(1MiB, 1MiB) was insufficient once an envelope wrapper pushed the line past the cap (ob-c90d58a1). Both are high-severity silent correctness failures that do not surface until E2E tests or real data are used.

use_when: writing property-based tests in Go against validated schemas, regex-constrained identifiers, or tightly constrained input spaces
content: Use constructive generators that assemble valid inputs by composition over constrained schemas; never add rejection filters or restrict generator ranges to make a failing property pass — instead, stop at the first shrunk counterexample, report it, and explicitly document and scope out any known-impossible inputs with a named exclusion comment.
causal_note: Rejection-based generators over constrained spaces exhaust their quota and silently stop exploring; narrowing a generator to avoid a failure ships a false-green test that proves nothing and masks a genuine bug the property exposed.

use_when: Implementing a command that installs hooks across multiple or all agent hook events at once (mass-install, --all-events, or similar)
content: Define and enforce an explicit telemetry-safe allowlist of hook events; exclude every active-control event (e.g. Claude's WorktreeCreate) where the hook's stdout is consumed as data by the agent rather than discarded — a silent exit-0 hook on those events breaks the feature without any error message.
causal_note: Some hook events gate or replace agent behavior using hook stdout (WorktreeCreate must print the new worktree path). A fire-and-forget telemetry hook installed there produces no output and silently disables the feature.

use_when: designing any link-tracking, freshness-checking, content-addressability, or bookkeeping feature that would annotate source or documentation files with computed hashes or state
content: Externalize all bookkeeping hashes and mutable state to an append-only sidecar file (e.g. a JSONL event log); never embed them inline in source or documentation files.
causal_note: Inline hash rewrites force every regeneration pass to touch files that have not logically changed. In one incident, 165 of 168 changed files were pure mechanical hash rewrites, making the one real authored change invisible and corrupting co-change analytics by creating false coupling signals between unrelated files.

use_when: adding concurrency to a previously single-threaded daemon, introducing new package import relationships, or reimplementing an existing subsystem that has a reference implementation
content: When adding concurrency to a single-threaded daemon, immediately add mutexes to all shared mutable state and prove correctness with go test -race before adding any other functionality — do not defer to a later retrofit. Encode package import constraints as executable layering tests (walk the dep graph with go list, fail on violations) rather than leaving them as documentation. When reimplementing an existing subsystem, write cross-surface parity tests that assert the new implementation's response shapes match the reference implementation before or alongside the code.
causal_note: Concurrency retrofits are painful and introduce data races that ship undetected (039 task). Import violations found late require invasive refactors (039 task). Behavioral divergence from the reference — e.g., directory-walk ordering — is invisible to tests written only against the new code (038 task).

use_when: Writing or reviewing a content-hash ID minting function in Go, especially for idempotent event-sourced or projection-based storage
content: Never make a content-hash ID minting function fully variadic. Require at least one content argument via a non-variadic first parameter (e.g., NewRuleID(first string, rest ...string)) or return an error/panic on empty input. A parts ...string signature compiles cleanly with zero args, mints a constant collision hash, and silently drops all-but-first events in any idempotency-by-ID-projection design — causing data loss with no compile error and no test failure.
causal_note: Zero-arg calls to NewRuleID compiled cleanly and minted the same constant ID for every missed caller; the projection then dropped all subsequent events as duplicates, silently losing data (ob-8e2befa1).

use_when: investigating CI failures on a feature branch, or starting a CI-repair task to fix a red pipeline
content: Before diagnosing CI failures on a feature branch, check whether the failing file appears in the branch diff; failures in files absent from the diff indicate drift on the base branch, not a regression introduced by the branch. Before starting a CI-repair task, run each pipeline step independently (not through the serial `make check` shortcut) to get the true total scope — a pipeline that short-circuits on the first failure dramatically understates the real debt.
causal_note: Pre-existing gofmt drift on main caused every descendant feature branch to show a red fmt-check gate on a file the branch never touched (ob-ca7460ad). Fixing only the gofmt layer in a serial pipeline then exposed ~54 golangci-lint errors that had been silently masked, causing scope to balloon mid-PR (ob-059fc00d).

use_when: creating an execution worktree, dispatching a subagent phase, or branching a feature from main in a Go workspace
content: Before creating any execution worktree or dispatching a subagent phase, verify the committed tree compiles by running `go build ./...` from a fresh checkout of `origin/main` — not from the primary working directory — to ensure no untracked files are silently satisfying references in committed code.
causal_note: Untracked source files in the primary checkout can satisfy imports and symbol references that exist in committed code, masking compiler errors. Every worktree branched from the committed tree fails to compile while the primary checkout with the untracked file builds fine, as in ob-02659b89 (high severity).

use_when: Writing a Go test that asserts on a field populated from env-var detection (session IDs, host IDs) and serialized with omitempty
content: Explicitly set every env var inside any test that asserts on a field populated from env-var detection (e.g., events.DetectSessionID()) and serialized with omitempty. Never rely on the ambient dev-shell environment. A clean CI runner will omit the field entirely, making the test pass locally while silently failing on CI — the test is checking the host environment, not the code.
causal_note: TestE2ELoopQuickstart asserted session_id appeared in gap rows; session_id is omitempty and resolves from env vars absent on CI, so the test passed locally and failed on clean runners (ob-57f70162).

use_when: writing or refactoring auto-ui event handlers, subscribe-on-mount hooks (useEffect with [] deps), or removing a write-only state mirror
content: Pass only stable module-level selectors to subscribe-on-mount hooks — never a closure that captures a component prop; key the component on the prop if a prop-parameterised selector is needed. When an event handler gates on a narrow condition (e.g., `!known`), explicitly verify whether known-path or already-seen-resource updates also need handling before shipping. Before deleting a write-only state mirror, enumerate every field it carried and prove each field survives under the replacement model, including param-less routes that may inadvertently re-derive and clear state.
causal_note: A prop-closing selector captured at mount time becomes stale after subsequent prop changes with no runtime error; a too-narrow event guard produces silent stale UI; deleting a state mirror silently breaks any field that relied on its structural persistence.

use_when: writing scanner tests, AST-pattern matcher tests, or golden-file tests for any language parser in auto-graph
content: Include at least one test fixture per common syntactic variant (e.g. single-quoted and double-quoted imports in TypeScript); generate golden files end-to-end through the same binary path a user invokes — never from intermediate internal representations — so that normalization passes and canonicalization are exercised before the golden is written.
causal_note: Double-quote-only fixtures allow single-quote sensitivity bugs to ship undetected; goldens generated from pre-canonicalization internal representations pass while asserting stale internal values instead of the public API contract.

use_when: dispatching subagents to write files in a shared git worktree, or verifying that a subagent phase completed successfully
content: Dispatch file-writing subagents serially, never concurrently, in a shared worktree. After each subagent reports completion, independently verify the expected files exist on disk (`git status`, `test -f`, `grep`) before the next agent starts or the step is marked done. When a subagent is killed mid-run, inspect the worktree for partial output first — if files were written, complete the phase from the coordinator rather than re-dispatching the same prompt. Never accept an agent's self-reported success as ground truth: silent write loss and hallucinated 'already done' are both real failure modes.
causal_note: Concurrent subagents sharing a worktree silently dropped ~7 out of 9 packages' Phase 2 edits with no error output (ob-0b5ff9c0). In the same session an agent claimed files were complete when git showed them unmodified (ob-019819f1). A separate session found that re-dispatching a killed subagent without inspecting the worktree wasted two retries — the files were already half-written (ob-bcb9949a). All three failure modes are eliminated by serial dispatch + on-disk verification.

use_when: writing acceptance criteria for an exclusion or filtering gate, or auditing a plan after a design decision has changed (e.g., a parameter removed, shared logic relocated)
content: Before accepting an exclusion gate's AC, trace at least one concrete instance of the thing to exclude through every 'keep' branch of the condition — the task's own Problem statement is the best counterexample. After any design decision resolves, audit all function signatures, test file names, and import lists in the plan for stale references before implementation begins; Go silently accepts unused function parameters, so a dead registry arg in an Ingest signature compiles and ships without warning.
causal_note: Task 043's AC-3 encoded the exact foreign-nested-clone leak the task existed to close, and it was unit-tested as correct; task 022's plan still declared a removed registry parameter in Ingest's signature that compiled silently and shipped as dead wiring — both caught only by PR review, not by the test runner (ob-fa7c9932 high-severity, ob-3115949b).

use_when: adding a callback, sink, or handler func field to a Go struct whose goroutine may be started before the field is assigned
content: Never store a mutable callback or event-sink as a plain `func` field on a struct whose Run goroutine can start before the field is wired; store it in `atomic.Value`, load it into a local variable per invocation, and invoke the local copy outside any existing mutex.
causal_note: Assigning a plain func field after goroutine start is a data race detected by the Go race detector; invoking a callback while holding a mutex risks lock-order inversion with any mutex the callback itself acquires.

use_when: writing or reviewing acceptance criteria that include e2e test coverage, or authoring e2e tests with performance assertions
content: Acceptance criteria that require e2e coverage must explicitly state the build-tag-aware invocation (e.g., `go test -tags=e2e ./e2e/`); `go test ./...` silently skips files guarded by `//go:build e2e`, making e2e ACs vacuously passable. Performance timing assertions in e2e tests must wrap only the production code path under measurement — test setup steps (repo clone, binary compile) must complete before the timer starts, or the assertion measures infrastructure, not the target operation.
causal_note: An e2e AC citing only `go test ./...` was passable without ever running the e2e suite because the tests were behind a `//go:build e2e` tag (ob-03798936). A performance assertion that included clone and compile time would be network/toolchain-dependent rather than measuring the operation it claimed to test (ob-51b8d087). Both were in the same codebase.

use_when: preparing to close or mark a task complete, especially tasks that are part of a larger epic
content: Before closing a task, explicitly check each acceptance criterion in plan.html against what actually shipped in the code; do not rely on the absence of failing tests as proof of completeness — features with no test coverage can silently omit planned scope and only surface during a downstream epic audit.
causal_note: A task can ship only part of its planned scope (e.g. the host-field portion of an epic that also defined a ctl.* event namespace) and be marked complete because nothing breaks. The missing scope then becomes a hidden gap discovered much later, requiring unplanned follow-up work.

use_when: adding any warning, unresolved-import notice, or configuration diagnostic to a CLI command that outputs JSON in auto-graph or any auto-* package
content: Write all diagnostics (unresolved imports, configuration warnings, scan errors) to stderr with structured fields (file, line, raw value, remediation hint); never add warning or diagnostic fields to the JSON output schema.
causal_note: Adding a warning field to the JSON graph schema couples process-level diagnostics to the data contract, breaks downstream parsers, and violates the project-wide rule that stdout is a strictly parseable payload.

use_when: writing conformance specs for reactive auto-ui components, or designing bus-event conformance tests that use `auto ui emit`
content: In each acceptance criterion for a reactive UI component, add an explicit note on what triggers an update (page load, reconnect, event-driven, or reload-required) and what does NOT update autonomously; before designing bus-event conformance tests, verify `auto ui emit` supports the required event types and envelope fields, and if it does not, document the `curl /api/rpc` workaround with its exact CloudEvents envelope shape in the conformance spec.
causal_note: Omitting update-trigger boundaries leads to false test assertions that the UI updates autonomously when it actually requires a reload; relying on `auto ui emit` without checking its capabilities leads to fragile manual curl workarounds that silently emit malformed envelopes.

use_when: adding mount-time RPC calls to any auto-ui component, or changing the SPA's default landing view to one that fetches on mount
content: Add a `whenOpen(): Promise<void>` readiness gate in rpc.js that delays mount-time fetches until the WebSocket is OPEN; call.() must not reject synchronously while the socket is still CONNECTING. When a component that makes RPC calls on mount becomes the default landing view, add a cold-load conformance assertion that verifies data arrives on first page open without a manual reload.
causal_note: Prevents a deterministic cold-load failure where every mount-time RPC call rejects with 'not connected' until the user manually reloads. The bug is latent while the landing view makes no mount-time calls and surfaces immediately when any component that fetches on mount is promoted to the default route.

use_when: developing or testing a no-build browser SPA served by Go's http.FileServer with an esm.sh import map
content: Apply three non-negotiable disciplines for no-build Preact/esm.sh SPAs: (1) prefix every transitive import-map entry with `*` (e.g. `"preact/hooks": "https://esm.sh/*preact@10.x.x/hooks"`) so nested imports inside esm.sh-fetched modules route back through the map and do not produce duplicate framework instances; (2) wrap `http.FileServer` in middleware that injects `Cache-Control: no-store` so browsers do not replay cached ES modules after a server change; (3) treat the browser conformance step as a mandatory acceptance gate — Go unit tests are structurally incapable of catching module-resolution, import-map, or HTTP-caching failures.
causal_note: All three gaps produced blank-page or silently-broken regressions that `go test` reported as passing: duplicate Preact instances broke stateful hooks with no error, cached modules hid server changes visible only to curl, and module-resolution failures were invisible to Go tests but broke every user-visible AC.

use_when: writing Go helper functions intended for use in a subsequent commit, or planning multi-phase Go implementation commits
content: Never commit Go helper functions as an isolated phase ahead of their callers; always include the consuming call sites in the same commit so that the unused-symbol lint check in the pre-commit hook passes on every intermediate state.
causal_note: ob-f9820760: committing resolveRoot, cleanDocPath, and other helpers before their callers caused `unused` lint failures in the pre-commit hook; the only fix was to merge the isolated helpers commit with the consuming phase into a single commit.

use_when: writing Go tests that require network access, external binary cloning, or other slow/online operations
content: Gate every network-dependent or long-running Go test behind a `//go:build e2e` build tag so that `go test ./...` stays offline-safe and fast by default; document the explicit `-tags=e2e` invocation in the package CLAUDE.md and Makefile target.
causal_note: Without the build tag, a single network-dependent test forces the default test run online, breaks CI in air-gapped environments, and slows every local test cycle — all silently, because the test appears to belong to the normal suite.

use_when: dispatching multiple subagents to implement phases of a task, or considering running parallel phases in the same git worktree
content: Never dispatch concurrent subagents into the same git worktree: pre-commit hooks that run formatters over all source files (e.g., goimports) auto-stage untracked work from parallel phases into the wrong commit; concurrent tool runs (e.g., `npx skills install`) silently overwrite committed-correct generated files. Dispatch phases serially, and before staging generated files (e.g., `.agents/skills/`, `skills-lock.json`) diff them against HEAD to detect regressions introduced by concurrent processes.
causal_note: ob-9e3f0904: concurrent Phase 1 and Phase 2 subagents in the same worktree caused goimports (run by the pre-commit hook over all files) to auto-stage Phase 2's untracked files into Phase 1's commit, corrupting attribution. ob-f91feec1: a concurrent `npx skills install` silently reverted a committed fix (`auto search` → `autosearch`) with stale generated content; the pre-commit stale-ref guard was the only safety net and the agent nearly committed the regression.

use_when: implementing or reviewing a proxy layer that decodes routing selectors from JSON or performs format conversion between upstream and downstream contracts
content: In a proxy routing decoder, enumerate every field-name alias documented in the protocol spec (both camelCase and snake_case variants) and add an explicit test for each alias; perform format conversions (e.g., base64 → raw bytes) inside the proxy layer so the client-facing contract stays byte-identical; for RPC proxy unit tests, inject a DialFunc backed by `net.Pipe` peers rather than real sockets to achieve full API-level coverage without binding ports or spawning subprocesses.
causal_note: A missing alias silently routes all requests using the documented name to the wrong backend with no error; leaving format conversion to the client forces unnecessary client-side changes and breaks the documented contract; real-socket tests add subprocess/port overhead that `net.Pipe` eliminates.

use_when: registering a shared handler struct or dispatcher onto multiple peer connections in an RPC or WebSocket server
content: Never store per-connection state (subscription cancel func, session context, user identity, auth token) in a shared handler struct. Hold it exclusively in the accept-loop closure that owns the peer's lifetime. A single shared handler instance has no per-connection identity, so state written there is overwritten on each new connection.
causal_note: A shared handler instance registered onto every peer caused subscription cancel funcs to be overwritten on each new connection, leaking subscriptions and making cancel impossible — found in the 040 event-ingest-relay task.

use_when: implementing a --full rebuild flag for an ETL source that has its own external sync-state file, or writing a fixture-generation script that invokes an incremental ETL tool
content: Wire `--full` to delete ALL incremental state for the source — including external sync-state files (e.g., `~/.auto/etl/git/sync-state.json`) — not only the output directory. For fixture-generation scripts, run the ETL tool under an isolated temp HOME so no pre-existing sync-state file suppresses output on developer machines that have already indexed the target dataset.
causal_note: A --full flag that only removed the output dir left the seen-SHA set intact, causing every commit to be treated as already-seen and producing zero rows with no error — indistinguishable from a successful incremental run; fixture scripts sharing the developer's HOME produced partial or empty snapshots on machines with prior state (ob-2fdc70d0, ob-4d6ac5f6 across two sessions).

use_when: designing or extending the RPC handler layer in autowatch or auto-ui, or adding new lifecycle or control-plane event types to the hub
content: Keep RPC handlers thin: validate params, then delegate entirely to exported service methods. Emit lifecycle events (start, reap, cancel) from shared service primitives — e.g., startWorker/Reap — not from individual callers or dispatch paths. Gate control-plane events at the hub.Broadcast call site rather than at relay bridges so bridges can unconditionally forward everything on the hub without per-type filtering.
causal_note: Fat handlers violate layering constraints and make unit tests hard. Caller-level emission duplicates or silently drops events when multiple paths exist (039 task). Relay-level gating scatters filtering logic and couples bridge code to event semantics (040 task).

use_when: adding a new value to an enumerated set (message roles, tool kinds, status codes) that has validator functions in multiple packages, or adding rows to a test fixture that is shared across multiple test files in auto-search
content: Consolidate duplicated value-whitelist functions into a single shared package-level constant or function — never maintain parallel copies across packages. When a test fixture is shared across multiple test files, centralise any absolute-count assertion in a single constant or helper, or switch to relative assertions (`got == before+N`) so that adding fixture rows requires exactly one change.
causal_note: ob-5a62123d: `normalizeRole` existed independently in `search/messages.go` and `stats/validate.go`; adding `thinking` to one copy while missing the other caused `stats --role thinking` to be rejected on the missed path. ob-7513761b: adding 4 fixture rows to exercise a new code path required hunting and updating more than 10 hard-coded count assertions spread across 5 test files.

use_when: refactoring Cobra init()-based commands into NewXxxCmd() constructors, or adding boolean CLI flags to commands with expected default-on behaviors
content: When extracting Cobra init() registrations into a NewXxxCmd() constructor, every sub-constructor (newRunCmd, newServeCmd, etc.) must allocate a fresh cobra.Command value internally — never mutate a package-level *cobra.Command variable — so that calling the constructor twice (as test harnesses do) does not panic with 'flag redefined'. Separately, after drafting any boolean flag, audit its Default value against the acceptance criteria: a `false` default silently voids a 'default-enabled' AC with no compile or test failure.
causal_note: Package-level cobra.Command + re-registration panics on the second call, which integration tests trigger by building the command tree per test case. False boolean defaults silently create no-op production installs when the AC requires the behavior to be on by default. Both failure modes are invisible to the compiler.

use_when: embedding arbitrary Go-marshalled JSON into an HTML <script> block — in any template or string-builder that injects model data into a page
content: Never use Go's default json.Marshal to produce JSON for <script> injection. Always: (1) create an encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false), (2) explicitly replace every `</` with `<\/` and every U+2028/U+2029 with their escape sequences in the resulting bytes, and (3) make this a standalone tested helper function — not an inline ad-hoc step.
causal_note: ob-0a7c6a11: Go's default HTML-escape mode silently corrupts JSON containing `</script>`, breaking page parsing. The fix requires both disabling HTML escape AND explicit `</` replacement, because SetEscapeHTML(false) alone still leaves U+2028/U+2029 line separators that break script context.

use_when: writing a Go test that must detect a bug before a fix and still pass after it, especially when the fix alters internal function signatures
content: Restrict the test to the exported public API and on-disk filesystem observations only; never call unexported functions or depend on internal signatures that the fix may rename or change. The test must compile identically against both buggy and fixed code.
causal_note: A fix that renames or re-signs an internal function (e.g. planPrune) causes compilation failure for any test that called it directly, breaking the build between the 'bug detected' and 'bug fixed' states and defeating the purpose of the regression test.

use_when: consuming WebSocket messages, JSON-RPC notifications, or any typed event envelope in UI JavaScript or Go — especially when the event carries a nested data or params wrapper
content: Never read payload fields directly off an envelope object (e.g. ev.path or params.path). Always route reads through a single typed parser function (e.g. parseDocChanged) that knows the exact nesting path. Pin the nesting contract with a backend serialization test so no consumer can silently regress when the envelope structure changes.
causal_note: When WebSocket events nest the payload under ev.data and JSON-RPC notifications nest it under params.data, direct field access at the wrong level is always undefined — the subscription silently never matches, making liveness a no-op in production. A single parser function is the only reliable single source of truth for the correct access path.

use_when: writing a shell hook that calls a CLI subcommand, extending an existing hook command to emit output, or designing hooks that fire across multiple agent platforms (Claude, Codex)
content: Before wiring a hook to a CLI subcommand: (1) grep the command's `Flags()` registrations to confirm each flag used in the hook stanza exists on that exact subcommand — do not assume a flag is present because a sibling command has it; (2) check whether the hook command has an established no-stdout invariant and scope any new output strictly to the event types that support responses, adding an AC that all other installed events remain silent; (3) for cross-agent hooks, verify each agent's PostToolUse trigger semantics from upstream docs rather than assuming a shared schema — Claude splits success/failure into PostToolUse vs PostToolUseFailure, while Codex fires PostToolUse on all completions with a different payload shape.
causal_note: ob-57feb89d: hook stanzas called `auto skill sync --check --format json` but `sync` registered no `--format` flag (only `--text`), producing silent no-ops or pre-commit crashes caught only by Codex review, not by stub-based tests. ob-2c8319fb: Task 020 required `auto hooks fire` to be a pure observer (exit 0, no stdout); adding hookSpecificOutput JSON would break Codex Stop/SubagentStop events that reject non-empty stdout. ob-0cf2f402: a design assumed a uniform `is_error` field on PostToolUse payloads — upstream docs show the field does not exist on Claude PostToolUse and has a different shape on Codex.

use_when: a Go module in the monorepo needs to consume types or functions defined in another module's internal/ packages
content: Add thin pkg/ wrapper packages in the exporting module (type aliases plus delegating functions) rather than promoting internal/ paths or moving types into a shared module — this preserves the internal/ visibility contract, requires zero changes to the exporting module's existing call sites, and composes cleanly with go.work replace directives.
causal_note: Go's internal/ rule is a hard compiler error for cross-module imports of internal/ paths; the minimum-blast-radius fix is wrapping at the exporting side, which avoids restructuring the owning module or creating a new shared module just for type exposure.

use_when: writing Go config accessor functions (Get, Read, Quietly variants) or OS-bootstrapped init helpers such as EnsureHost
content: Config accessor functions for constrained values (host IDs, tokens, format-validated strings) must validate the stored value against the same format regex used at write time, not merely check for emptiness — a missing value is an expected error, but an invalid format silently returned is a data-corruption bug. EnsureHost-style init helpers must treat each OS API call as independently failable: generate the composite default only when all calls succeed, fall back to a bare hostname if user.Current() fails, and fall back further if even the bare value fails format validation.
causal_note: A 'quiet' accessor that skips regex validation allows hand-edited invalid config to propagate silently onto bus events or outbound API calls. Composite hostname+username defaults silently break in containerized environments where /etc/passwd is absent.

use_when: adding registry-based filtering to a Go ETL command or CLI tool that reads the project registry to decide which repos to process
content: Gate registry filtering at the cmd layer where both path and remote are available; pass gated slices/maps to internal packages and keep those packages registry-agnostic. Use a quiet read-only load (stat + LoadProjects, return empty on error) rather than EnsureProjects, which mutates the registry as a side effect of being called. Limit path-prefix matching to workspaces with no origin remote — genuine subdirectories of registered projects already match by remote, so an unconditional prefix match exclusively admits foreign nested clones.
causal_note: Applying registry gates inside internal packages breaks testability and separation of concerns; calling EnsureProjects from ETL mutates the user's registry as a side effect; unconditional path-prefix matching passes foreign nested repos through the gate, defeating the filter's entire purpose (ob-26499dae, ob-c114e844, ob-a488588b across two sessions).

use_when: running or debugging lint failures in a Go worktree, especially when errors reference file paths that look unfamiliar or from other branches
content: Use `golangci-lint run` (not just `go vet`) as the post-phase lint gate — it catches `ineffassign` and other issues that `go vet` silently ignores. If golangci-lint reports errors referencing file paths outside the current worktree (e.g., paths matching a deleted sibling task worktree), run `golangci-lint cache clean` before treating any failure as real; the shared on-disk cache retains stale analysis entries for paths that no longer exist.
causal_note: A deleted sibling worktree's paths remained in the shared golangci-lint cache, causing a clean branch to appear to have lint failures pointing at non-existent files (ob-b7999514). In a separate task, a subagent's iterative variable rewrite left an `ineffassign` that `go vet` passed but golangci-lint caught, surfacing only at the lint gate (ob-2812d835).

use_when: Implementing or testing a git hook installer, or writing E2E verification for any CLI command that installs hooks or wires bare command strings into agent configs
content: Apply three checks: (a) Use git rev-parse --git-common-dir (not --git-dir) to locate the shared hooks directory — --git-dir returns a per-worktree path in linked worktrees. (b) Before dogfooding any installer that creates directories under a dot-path (.codex, .claude), verify those paths are not stray files in the repo with ls -la. (c) When verifying an installed bare command string, invoke it via sh -c '<command>' after setting PATH — calling ./bin/<binary> directly passes even when the bare installed string would fail due to PATH not including the binary.
causal_note: Three independent installer failures share the same pattern of untested real-world resolution: --git-dir installs hooks in the wrong directory for linked worktrees; a stray 0-byte committed file at an expected directory path produces 'not a directory' errors that look like installer bugs; and invoking the binary by local path rather than the installed command string masks PATH resolution failures entirely.

use_when: Adding a new lifecycle value, kind, or tag to a shared valid-set in Go, or writing a new command that calls a shared validate() function
content: Put all cross-field invariants (e.g., field A present implies field B must be set; new lifecycle member implies provenance path is required) in the shared validate() function, not in per-command handlers. After adding a member to any shared valid-set, immediately trace every command that now reaches that member through the shared enum check, and introduce the matching guard in validate() rather than in the individual command.
causal_note: Per-command guards are bypassed by every other command entry point: an enforced lifecycle invariant placed only in the graduate handler was silently skipped by create and edit (ob-83282db2). Adding 'enforced' to validLifecycles then let create/edit bypass the provenance gate entirely (ob-e1607e80).

use_when: writing a Go test that must simulate a stale Unix socket — a socket file present on disk with no live server behind it
content: Use net.ListenUnix with ln.SetUnlinkOnClose(false) to keep the socket path on disk after the listener is closed. Do not use net.Listen("unix", path) — it auto-unlinks the socket file on close, making stale-file simulation impossible and producing a false pass or wrong behavior.
causal_note: Go's net.Listen("unix", ...) removes the socket file on close, so tests written with it found no file and either false-passed or exercised a completely different code path than the stale-socket scenario they were designed to cover.

use_when: emitting a stored git remote URL to any browser, bus event, log, or RPC response boundary
content: Apply `git.NormalizeRemoteURL` defensively on every code path that emits a stored remote URL to a browser, bus, or log boundary — never assume the value in the registry is already credential-free. Any handler that re-emits stored registry data must normalize it itself, even if the writer appeared to normalize on insert.
causal_note: ob-82ca803e: the `project.list` handler re-emitted stored registry remotes directly to the browser, leaking embedded credentials, because it trusted the stored value was already clean — unlike `FindProjectByRemote` which normalized both sides defensively.

use_when: implementing a prune or GC command for a global shared cache, or implementing archive extraction that writes to a destination directory that may already contain files
content: For global shared cache GC: build the referenced-IDs set by iterating the global project registry (e.g. `~/.auto/projects.json` via LoadProjects) — not just the current project's lock file — so entries still needed by other registered projects are never deleted. For archive extraction: replace `os.MkdirAll` with a component-by-component `Lstat` walk that rejects any symlink found along the path, including symlinks already present in the destination directory before extraction begins.
causal_note: Using only the local lock file for a global prune deletes cache entries still needed by sibling projects, breaking their offline builds (ob-958c9fec); `os.MkdirAll` silently follows pre-existing symlinks in the destination, enabling directory traversal past the entry-validation boundary that was supposed to be the security perimeter (ob-b3c4f8b8).

use_when: staging a large batch of auto-generated or mechanical files for a commit while needing to exclude one or a few specific files
content: Stage a large batch while excluding specific files with `git add -A && git reset -q -- <excluded-file>` rather than individually enumerating hundreds of paths; the excluded files remain cleanly unstaged and can be committed separately with their own message.
causal_note: ob-2e12b7ca: individually staging 167 mechanical files is error-prone; the add-then-reset pattern reliably commits the batch while leaving real-content edits in a distinct commit.

use_when: declaring a Go implementation phase done, writing per-phase verification steps, or configuring CI job commands for a Go module
content: Run `make check` (or `golangci-lint run ./...`) in every per-phase verify step — `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test` are necessary but not sufficient; linters such as `modernize`, `gosec`, and `nilerr` surface real defects that standard tooling skips. Never declare a phase done without a passing full lint gate.
causal_note: Omitting golangci-lint from intermediate phase gates lets lint debt accumulate silently and then block the final gate with a large batch of findings — 27 golangci-lint findings batched into Phase 4 in ob-927fd7f8, and a real `modernize` finding missed entirely by go vet/test in ob-cd123021.

use_when: adding an explicit/fast-path branch alongside a default/walk branch, or shipping a new interface, resolver, or security gate whose tests use a fake or mock implementation
content: When adding an explicit/fast-path branch: enumerate every normalization, deduplication, and validation step the default path runs and apply each one explicitly in the fast path too. When shipping a unit-tested interface or security gate with fake implementations: grep every production call site to confirm a real, non-nil implementation is constructed and passed; for security gates that take an allow-list parameter, verify the list is populated from project configuration at the call site — never left as nil.
causal_note: Unit tests pass because fakes are wired correctly, but production silently skips the feature or gate: explicit path skips dedup causing last-writer-wins data corruption (ob-d140cd19); nil interface at production call site silently bypasses a deep-link feature (ob-f1593cc4); nil allow-list at the call site permanently disables a non-TTY/CI security opt-in gate (ob-0863c679).

use_when: implementing or auditing a CLI verb that should apply/mutate/write data (e.g. update, sync, apply, prune, delete), or when a deletion command uses symbolic keys (style names, IDs, names) to locate targets
content: Before closing any task that introduces a mutating CLI verb: (1) read the implementation of the engine function called and confirm it actually writes to disk — not just builds a plan — by checking whether it rewrites the lock file, materialises the commit, or renders targets; (2) for commands that delete or prune by symbolic key, trace the key through the write-path code (not the design doc) and confirm the key convention used at deletion time matches the key convention used at write time.
causal_note: Prevents silent no-ops where acceptance tests pass vacuously: a plan-only engine sibling satisfies the literal criterion while writing nothing (ob-4cbd7ebc); a key convention mismatch causes an empty scan so the 'deletion succeeded' AC is trivially satisfied with nothing removed (ob-5626fb55).

use_when: writing a long-running Go server, daemon, or watch command using Cobra
content: Wire signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) inside the individual serve/watch Cobra command's RunE function, not in main.go. main.go passes context.Background() which never cancels, making any signal handling placed there dead code. Always pass a context.WithTimeout deadline to srv.Shutdown() to prevent it from blocking indefinitely.
causal_note: Signal handling in main.go is silently unreachable because Cobra receives a non-cancellable Background context; the server must be force-killed rather than shutting down cleanly. The bug produces no compile or test failure.

use_when: Writing code that reads a git remote URL from a project registry, config file, or git output and then broadcasts, logs, or transmits it to any external consumer (bus events, UI clients, network envelopes)
content: Always call NormalizeRemoteURL() to strip embedded credentials (https://token:@...) from any git remote URL before it enters a bus event, log, network envelope, or stored registry entry; add a unit test asserting the emitted remote contains no '@' or credential substring.
causal_note: Raw git remote URLs frequently embed live PATs (e.g. https://x-access-token:github_pat_11AB35...@github.com/...). Broadcasting the raw URL on an event bus or writing it to a log leaks those credentials to every connected client and log consumer.

use_when: designing a two-binary producer/consumer system where both binaries need to parse or normalize the same file format or event envelope
content: Before writing either binary, identify all normalization and extraction logic that both sides need and place it in a shared internal module (e.g., auto-shared); never define shared logic in package main, as it cannot be imported by any other module and silently forces the consuming binary to re-implement it.
causal_note: auto-cli's `extractPaths`, `stringField`, and `buildHookEvent` lived in package main, so auto-etl could not import them; the ETL 'reuse' claim in the plan was false and only surfaced during code review (ob-9e9053d9).

use_when: context.md or a plan references APIs or symbols from a dependency that was marked 'planned' or 'not yet merged' at planning time
content: At execution start, grep for every symbol the plan references from 'planned-not-merged' dependencies; read the actual merged files and adapt to the real signatures before writing any code. The implementation contract is what matters, not the identifier that was planned against.
causal_note: Context docs snapshot planned APIs at planning time; the moment those dependencies merge, the snapshot becomes stale. Executors who trust the plan discover wrong signatures mid-implementation (e.g. `skill.ParseLock` taking `[]byte` instead of a loader package, `sync.Run` vs the planned `sync.Update`), forcing silent adaptation or re-architecture.

use_when: about to call the Edit tool on any file
content: Always call Read on a file before calling Edit in the same session. The Edit tool enforces this sequencing constraint and will raise an immediate error if Read was skipped, requiring an extra round-trip before the write can proceed.
causal_note: Skipping Read before Edit is a hard tool invariant: the edit is blocked until Read is run, wasting a full round-trip (ob-3276644c). In long agentic chains this compounds latency and can break sequencing assumptions downstream.

use_when: implementing or debugging a multi-source ETL command that runs several sub-sources and aggregates their results into a single process exit
content: Report per-source exit status separately and exit non-zero only when the explicitly targeted source fails. Never collapse all sub-source failures into a single aggregate exit code; provide `--only <source>` for callers that need a clean signal for one source.
causal_note: A single 404 from an unrelated github sub-source caused `autoetl run --full` to exit 1 even though the in-scope sessions transform had successfully processed 809 sessions, making it impossible to distinguish a target-source failure from an unrelated sub-source error (ob-56802d3a).

use_when: adding, removing, or renaming columns in an ETL parquet schema, or abandoning a feature branch that wrote parquet partitions
content: Default new tool-output or envelope columns to a single raw JSON TEXT/STRING parquet field rather than typed per-field columns; this isolates the schema from upstream format changes and lets DuckDB json_extract handle derived analytics. When typed schema changes are unavoidable, bump model.SchemaVersion on any branch that emits new columns and revert or re-ingest orphaned partitions before abandoning the branch — DuckDB NULL-fill silently hides cross-partition column drift until a full --full backfill is required.
causal_note: An abandoned branch left orphaned columns (tool_use_id, duration_ms, interrupted) in one weekly partition; DuckDB hid the drift invisibly in normal queries, requiring a full backfill to remediate (ob-51432633). Typed envelope columns lock the schema to whatever the producer emits today, so any field addition triggers cross-partition drift on future changes (ob-9e9f39df).

use_when: implementing a multi-stage pipeline with a scanner phase and a separate consumer/builder phase (e.g. file-walker + graph builder, AST scanner + context-pack builder) in the auto-graph or any auto-* package
content: Define all cross-stage constants (import-kind names, edge labels, skip-path lists) in one shared package imported by both producer and consumer; add a canonicalization shim at the boundary if the producer is external or legacy; and require at least one integration test that exercises the full path from real scanner output through the consumer — never rely on synthetic unit tests alone at this seam.
causal_note: String literal mismatches between scanner and builder, divergent skip lists between the file-walker and scanner, and synthetic unit tests with auto-generated goldens all produce silently wrong output (zero-edge graphs, misclassified edges, hidden interface bugs) with no error signal — only an integration test using real scanner output surfaces them.

use_when: writing Go tests for ETL transforms, especially negative-path assertions or comparisons between two systems that store data in different formats
content: For negative-path assertions, write `if badConditionHolds { t.Error(...) }` — never `if !condition { t.Log("ok") }`, which is a no-op on the failure path and will always pass. For cross-system format comparisons (e.g., SSH vs HTTPS remote URLs, flat vs partitioned parquet paths), feed each side of the assertion its actual production-format value; pre-normalizing both inputs to the same format hides the format-mismatch bug that only exists in production.
causal_note: An inverted `!condition + t.Log` assertion passed regardless of whether the invariant was violated, caught only by automated PR review; pre-normalized test inputs for SSH/HTTPS URL comparison made tests pass while production code silently failed on the format difference (ob-c821f403 high-severity, ob-cca3fa9e across two sessions).

use_when: reading a git remote URL to store in parquet, a log file, a JSON event, or any other persistent format
content: Always call StripCredentials() (or equivalent) on every git remote URL before writing it to any output format — parquet, JSONL, JSON, logs. The spec will not mention credential stripping; apply it defensively at the normalize layer, not at individual call sites, so it cannot be skipped.
causal_note: git remote get-url origin returned x-access-token:github_pat_...@github.com URLs that flowed unstripped into both repo_remote and repo_remote_normalized parquet columns (ob-11620ba6). Only E2E testing against a real repo caught the leak before ship. Specs consistently omit this requirement.

use_when: Processing a hook payload JSON object that includes a cwd field alongside relative file paths or tool paths
content: Always resolve relative tool paths and run git operations (RepoRoot, Provenance) against the payload's cwd field, not the hook process's working directory — pass cwd explicitly to every git call, never default to os.Getwd().
causal_note: The hook process cwd and the payload cwd can differ silently (e.g. the hook binary is invoked from a different directory), causing rel to be computed against the wrong root so that downstream path matchers like docs/** miss all events.

use_when: creating a worktree branch, rebasing a feature branch onto main, or working in a multi-agent environment where parallel PRs may be in flight
content: Run `git fetch origin && git pull origin main` immediately before creating a worktree branch. After rebasing, run `git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline` and diff the incoming commits against your local changes — a parallel PR may have already landed the same fix, making your local production copy redundant; drop superseded hunks rather than carrying duplicates to the PR.
causal_note: Forking from a stale local main causes mid-task rebase conflicts (ob-1a633a08: import-graph PR landed after worktree forked; ob-f9b834bb: planning-doc commit caused add/add rebase conflicts) and silent work duplication (ob-78ab4bf9: PR #112 merged the complete prune fix while the agent was re-implementing it, creating a conflicting PR).

use_when: designing a keepalive or peer-reap watchdog for any server-push or read-only subscriber protocol, or writing liveness/reap tests
content: Design bidirectional ping/pong from the start for any protocol where clients are read-only consumers; a unidirectional server-ping watchdog cannot distinguish a dead peer from a healthy silent one on a reliable transport. For every positive 'dead peer reaped' assertion, add a bounded negative assertion that a healthy-but-app-idle peer survives past the same timeout, and make the dead simulation genuinely different from an idle peer — sever the connection or wedge reads, do not just go silent.
causal_note: A unidirectional watchdog false-reaps healthy silent consumers (ob-0769b2d9). A silent-peer 'dead' simulation is behaviorally identical to a healthy read-only consumer, so a test asserting the watchdog fires proves the bug, not the intended behavior (ob-55a184e8).

use_when: creating a feature branch or git worktree, especially in the auto-stack monorepo where a pre-commit hook or daemon may advance main between sessions
content: Before creating a feature branch or worktree, always run `git fetch origin && git push origin main` to confirm local main is fully in sync with origin. A local main that is ahead of origin — even by a few hook-generated commits — produces a PR diff polluted with unrelated commits that GitHub cannot auto-correct; recovery requires pushing main and patching the PR base via the GitHub API.
causal_note: A worktree branched from a local main that was 3 commits ahead of origin caused 140+ unrelated files to appear in the PR diff (ob-1626dcf1). The auto-stack pre-commit hook and dogfooding daemon routinely advance main between sessions, making this a recurring risk.

use_when: storing or comparing git URLs or file:// URIs as canonical identities, building a trust endpoint from a parsed URL, or detecting whether a filesystem path is a git repository root to record as a clonable source
content: When storing a git source as a clonable URL: resolve the true repository root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and store any directory remainder as a separate Subpath field — never store the original subdirectory path as the clone target. When building a canonical identity string from a parsed URL: explicitly handle file:// (host is always the empty string; path carries the full identity) and write an isolated unit test for every supported URL scheme before shipping.
