causal_note: Storing a subdirectory as the clone URL produces an unclonable reference at sync time (ob-1fa243cb); using only the URL host component for file:// URLs collapses all local repositories to the same identity, silently granting cross-repository trust (ob-ef2262c4).

use_when: golangci-lint reports findings at file paths that no longer exist on disk, or after removing a sibling worktree while another branch is active
content: When `golangci-lint` reports findings whose file paths point at a non-existent directory or a removed sibling worktree, run `golangci-lint cache clean` before re-running lint; treat the original findings as stale cache artifacts rather than real defects on the current branch.
causal_note: golangci-lint maintains a shared on-disk cache that retains analysis entries for files from deleted worktrees, producing phantom CI-blocking failures on what is actually a clean branch — as in ob-f2c8b167 where gosec findings referenced a non-existent `auto-stack-task-016/` directory.

use_when: writing code that prefix-matches, correlates by text, or serializes a field that has both a full-length and a truncated/preview variant (e.g. session intent, commit message body, any preview column in a list row vs a detail row)
content: Always fetch the full-length variant of a text field when performing prefix or substring matching — never use the truncated list-row preview. When both forms appear in CLI JSON output, give each a distinct key name (e.g. `first_user_intent` for the full value, `first_user_intent_preview` for the truncated one) so consumers cannot silently receive different shapes under one key.
causal_note: ob-4b47b9aa: sub-agent correlation by prompt-prefix silently broke for any child session whose intent exceeded 200 chars because the preview from SessionListRow was used instead of the full string from GetSessionByID. ob-7425655f: `session list` and `session describe` both emitted `first_user_intent` but with incompatible lengths, making downstream parsing non-deterministic depending on which command the consumer called.

use_when: writing a CLI command that resolves a user-supplied name, identifier, or path argument to a filesystem location
content: Validate every user-supplied identifier against its canonical name regex (e.g. `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`) before constructing any `filepath.Join` call; reject the request with a clear error if the identifier contains `..`, `/`, or any separator character.
causal_note: Passing a raw CLI argument directly into filepath.Join allows path-traversal attacks — e.g. `auto skill get ../../../tmp/leak --target claude` reads SKILL.md files outside the managed skills tree with no indication of the escape.

use_when: creating events, records, or domain entities that are derived as a pure function of their inputs, especially when multiple independent code paths may derive the same logical item
content: Assign deterministic IDs to any derived event or entity — e.g., a stable hash of source id + event type + relation — never random UUIDs. This ensures independently-produced copies of the same logical item collide on ID so a single dedup gate at any layer can suppress duplicates without per-path coordination.
causal_note: Random IDs on derived events silently defeated consumer-side id-dedup: auto-ui's local /api/rpc derive and autowatch's derive both called NewEvent with a fresh random ID, so two doc.changed events passed the gate and consumers saw duplicates — found in the 045 task.

use_when: adding a new Go package to the monorepo, or committing test fixtures in a package with a testdata directory
content: When creating a new Go package in the monorepo, immediately add a per-package gitignore entry for its in-place compiled binary (e.g., `auto-foo/auto`) — generic top-level patterns like `bin/` or `dist/` do not match binaries built inside package subdirectories. When a package needs committed test fixtures, add explicit negation entries for every distinct testdata subtree it uses (e.g., `!auto-graph/testdata/` AND `!auto-graph/e2e/testdata/`) — the repo-wide `**/testdata/` rule blocks all nested paths and a single top-level negation does not cascade.
causal_note: A 42 MB compiled binary accumulated as untracked noise because generic gitignore patterns missed the in-place build location (ob-3d6c754c). In the same repo, committed e2e fixtures for both `testdata/` and `e2e/testdata/` were silently ignored by the root `**/testdata/` rule, causing CI to fail on a clean checkout while local tests passed (ob-ae40464b).

use_when: transitioning from solution design to implementation planning, or scripting CLI flags into a plan or quickstart doc
content: Before running /new-plan: (1) request a structured inline review of solution.md to catch architectural flaws while the phase breakdown is still fluid; (2) verify every CLI flag and subcommand the plan will script by running `<tool> --help`; (3) run a multi-persona user simulation against the draft CLI surface to surface missing contract cases (empty states, error vocabulary, snapshot persistence, read-only escapes) that review threads typically miss.
causal_note: Design defects caught after the plan is written force re-architecture of already-committed phases. CLI surfaces that do not exist cause silent divergence when executors adapt without updating the doc. Missing CLI contract cases discovered post-implementation require breaking changes to an already-shipped interface.

use_when: writing or extending HTTP handler tests for a handler that validates request headers (Content-Type, Origin, Authorization, etc.)
content: In HTTP handler test helpers, always set every header that a conformant client would send — including Content-Type and any auth headers — from the very first test case. Adding a new header-validation guard must only require adding negative test cases, not retrofitting every existing test.
causal_note: Tests written without required headers become mechanically broken the moment a corresponding validation guard is added. Every existing test then needs a retrofit instead of only a new negative case, increasing churn and risk of missing a regression.

use_when: writing or reviewing a Go reconnect loop, reconcile manager, or connection watchdog in autowatch or auto-ui
content: Bound every RPC or subscription call inside a reconnect/reconcile loop with context.WithTimeout. Model 'degraded' (transport up, post-connect setup failed) as a distinct state from 'disconnected' with its own bounded retry branch. Hook each connection's Serve/Read goroutine to atomically clear its liveness flag on exit so the next reconcile tick re-dials the slot rather than treating the closed peer as still-connected.
causal_note: Without timeouts a non-responding peer permanently wedges the reconcile goroutine. Without a degraded state a subscribe-failed peer is never retried. Without clearing the liveness flag on Serve exit a dead peer is served indefinitely — all three bugs were found across the 042 and 045 tasks.

use_when: writing table-rendering or CLI output formatting code that displays data from columns that may contain embedded newlines — commit message bodies, tool output, file content snippets
content: Sanitize embedded newlines inside the lowest-level single-responsibility formatting helper (e.g. a `truncSubject` or `formatCell` function), not at individual call sites. Include at least one fixture value with an embedded newline in the test suite — if every fixture uses single-line values, the rendering bug survives CI but fires on the first real record with a body.
causal_note: ob-7995e7c5: every test fixture used single-line commit subjects, so the multi-line-breaks-row bug was invisible in CI; it would have fired on the first real commit with a body. Fixing inside `truncSubject` protected all future callers automatically versus a call-site fix that would have left new callers unprotected.

use_when: implementing a localhost-bound HTTP handler that ingests events, hooks, or webhooks — especially when porting or adapting a guard from a sibling Go module's internal package
content: Apply all three localhost ingest guards in order: (1) bind to loopback only, (2) reject any request that carries an Origin header (CSRF), (3) require Content-Type: application/json. When a reference implementation lives in a sibling module's internal package and cannot be imported, enumerate every guard from that source and re-implement each one explicitly — internal package boundaries mean no guard propagates automatically.
causal_note: Loopback binding alone does not prevent CSRF: browsers can issue CORS-safelisted text/plain POSTs to 127.0.0.1 without triggering a preflight, so any page the user visits can forge events. Internal package semantics in Go prevent cross-module import, so guards that exist in one module's internal/ tree are silently absent when a new handler is created in another module unless the developer explicitly re-documents and re-implements them.

use_when: implementing any RPC or HTTP handler in auto-ui (or any auto-* server) that accepts a filesystem path from the client
content: Validate every client-supplied filesystem path against a known project registry allowlist before passing it to any filesystem operation, even when the server listens on loopback only. Loopback scope does not eliminate path-traversal risk — an unvalidated worktree path can be used to read arbitrary host files.
causal_note: A `doc.get`/`doc.list` handler that accepted an arbitrary worktree path without registry validation would allow any local process to read any host file via the RPC surface. Loopback-only binding is not a security boundary for path-traversal.

use_when: Designing or extending an event-sourced Go package where consumer packages import a shared events package
content: In event-sourced Go packages, define ALL payload sub-types — status enums, nested structs, domain value types — inside the events package itself, never in consumer packages. The dependency arrow must flow one way: consumers import events, events imports nothing from consumers. Any payload type placed in a consumer package that the events package also needs creates a compile-blocking import cycle.
causal_note: Placing Signals in the miner consumer package while events imported miner for AppendEvent and AckStatus created a compile-blocking cycle that required moving all payload sub-types back into the events package (ob-72d7ed43).

use_when: Filtering session or event records by 'current repository' in code that runs inside a worktree-based development workflow
content: Scope session and event records to the current repository by normalized git remote, not by workspace or cwd filesystem path. In a worktree workflow, each worktree has a distinct absolute path for the same repo; path-equality scoping fragments one repo's records into disjoint sets and silently misses the majority.
causal_note: Scoping by Workspace path would have split one repo's session queue into several disjoint queues — one per active worktree — effectively losing most of the repo's mined sessions (ob-5fd32408). A related normalization bug (ob-f245ee59) also arose from inconsistent remote URL treatment across code paths.

use_when: writing shell install or update scripts that run under `set -euo pipefail` and perform a post-install side-effect after the critical step has already succeeded (daemon restart, cache invalidation, service reload)
content: Guard every post-install side-effect command with `|| true` or an explicit `if … ; then … else echo 'warning: …' >&2; fi` block so that a transient failure degrades to a logged warning rather than aborting the script with a non-zero exit and misleading the user into thinking the primary step failed.
causal_note: When a daemon restart issued after a successful binary replacement fails transiently, `set -euo pipefail` aborts the whole script. The binary was already updated, but the user sees an error exit and believes the update failed — a false overall failure caused by a non-critical side effect.

use_when: preparing context.md for multi-phase subagent dispatch on any task that touches existing Go code
content: In context.md, enumerate every code site the plan touches with exact file path and line range; for patterns to mirror, name the specific existing function (with file:line) rather than describing the pattern abstractly; for shared utilities used by multiple callers, list every call-site so executors see the full multi-caller picture before they start writing.
causal_note: Without file:line anchors, each dispatched subagent spends its first tokens re-discovering the codebase instead of writing code. Naming abstract patterns instead of concrete functions leads to reinvention of already-solved logic (e.g. bounded-buffer write-pump). Omitting multi-caller context hides that a change will affect more sites than the one the executor is focused on.

use_when: writing liveness or invalidation-driven conformance tests for auto-ui, especially tests that emit `doc.changed` or similar bus events
content: Before emitting an invalidation signal, write the backing resource to disk (or to the store) first — the emit only posts the envelope and does not modify backing state, so a re-fetch will find nothing new if the resource is absent. When asserting monotonic render counters (data-revision, nonce, sequence numbers), snapshot the value before triggering the event and assert strictly-greater-than the snapshot rather than an absolute expected value.
causal_note: Prevents silent false-passes: an invalidation event with no backing resource causes the re-list to find nothing new, and a monotonic counter starting from a non-zero baseline (left by earlier navigation) will never equal the hardcoded absolute value asserted.

use_when: writing or reviewing task context docs for a multi-phase or subagent-delegated task
content: Task context docs must include: (1) verified line-number references to every key code site (not just file paths), (2) an explicit 'gotchas' section listing known wrong patterns alongside their correct alternatives, and (3) non-obvious function-level fallback/default behaviors near integration points (e.g., 'isRuntimeImport returns true when no import_kinds set — line 432'). These specifics reduce subagent re-exploration more than high-level structural descriptions.
causal_note: Without pinned line refs and explicit gotchas, subagents re-discover the same pitfalls each phase (ob-43340179: wrong subcommand names, positional signature risks). Without documented fallback behaviors, silent misclassification bugs go undetected because they are invisible to automated tests (ob-d207f7fd: lenient default triggered incorrect classifications).

use_when: writing Go code that creates or persists config files containing credentials, tokens, or secret keys
content: Never write credential or API-key config files through shared WriteJSONFile helpers that unconditionally apply mode 0644. Implement a dedicated WriteSecure function that: creates the parent directory at 0700, writes the file, then calls os.Chmod(path, 0600). Enforce the resulting file-mode bits with a unit test that stats the file after writing.
causal_note: Shared JSON helpers create world-readable 0644 files; any config storing an API key or access key is then readable by all local users, violating least-privilege. The bug is invisible at runtime.

use_when: adding a new Go module to the auto-stack monorepo, expanding the Makefile PROJECTS list, or auditing which modules are covered by aggregate CI gates
content: When introducing a new module, add it to every aggregate Makefile target (test, vet, lint, race) in the same PR it is created. When widening PROJECTS to include a previously-excluded module, run lint/vet/test locally on that module first and fix all findings before the PR that widens the scope; do not ship the PROJECTS change until the module is clean.
causal_note: A module absent from PROJECTS is silently excluded from all CI quality checks — the most critical shared concurrency module had never been tested in CI in ob-dba3a3d4. Adding a previously-excluded module later converts all accumulated technical debt into immediate CI blockers, as happened in ob-9495a21d.

use_when: writing test fixtures for pairing-based logic (tool_use_id, foreign-key joins), token/byte budget bound assertions, or directory-tree distance label assertions in auto-search or auto-etl
content: For pairing-based fixture rows, always include a complete originator+result pair — a standalone result row with no matching originator is silently skipped and gives false confidence that the code path is exercised. For budget/token assertions, generate the fixture first and measure the actual output size empirically, then set the bound. For tree-distance fixtures, compute every d-label arithmetically (d = up-segments-to-LCA + down-segments-from-LCA, basenames stripped from both paths) before writing assertions.
causal_note: ob-f16f47c1: a standalone role=tool Bash row with no tool_use_id was silently skipped by the builder, making the AC appear covered when it was a no-op. ob-eb6285e9: an initial hot-file fixture produced only 395 tokens under --all (below the 500 bound it was meant to exceed), so the passing assertion was vacuous. ob-72b37b7e: a one-level-shallow seed shifted all d-labels by one, causing incorrect fixture assertions that propagated silently.

use_when: writing new Go files in any auto-* package before the first commit, or renaming schema fields or config keys in a Go tool
content: Apply these four checks before committing new Go code: (1) use `errors.New("literal message")` instead of `fmt.Errorf("literal message")` and direct string concatenation instead of `fmt.Sprintf("%s", x)` to satisfy the perfsprint linter; (2) check the zero-new-runtime-deps policy before importing any external library — verify stdlib covers the need first (e.g. `os.Stdin.Stat()` with `ModeCharDevice` for TTY detection rather than `golang.org/x/term`); (3) when the tool owns a YAML config file, parse it with `yaml.Decoder.KnownFields(true)` — the direct analog of `json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()` — so unknown fields are rejected at load time; (4) after renaming any schema field or config key, run the full integration-test suite before committing, because doctor/validate commands embed field-name strings as literals that silently become stale.
causal_note: Avoids a fixup-commit cycle: perfsprint failures surface at CI time instead of author time (ob-9af6d975); external dep import requires a full revert of go.mod/go.sum (ob-ee9c78d6); silent schema drift is caught at load time rather than at runtime with strict YAML parsing (ob-7f33ab32); stale field-name strings in doctor commands are the fastest class of breakage caught by integration tests (ob-4901891a).

use_when: parsing structured config or data files (JSONC, go.mod, tsconfig.json, YAML) line-by-line or via regex transformation to extract values or strip non-standard syntax
content: Strip inline comments and unquote values as the first step before field extraction; if transforming structured text (e.g. stripping JSONC comments), implement a single-pass state machine that tracks whether the cursor is inside a string rather than chaining independent regex passes over the same text.
causal_note: A two-pass regex approach (strip comments then strip trailing commas) matches structural patterns inside string values and silently corrupts data; naive line parsing that ignores inline comments or quoted module paths silently produces zero-edge or empty graphs with no error.

use_when: scripting any CLI command inside a plan step, acceptance criterion, or rollout note
content: Before writing any CLI subcommand into a plan step or AC rollout note, run `<binary> --help` (or `<binary> <subcommand> --help`) to confirm the exact subcommand name and required flags. Never infer subcommand names from the binary name, package name, or a similar project's conventions.
causal_note: Planning docs that reference a non-existent subcommand (e.g., `autoetl transform` when the real surface is `autoetl run`) cause every downstream E2E verification step to fail as written, forcing unplanned rework during execution (ob-daad82b6).

use_when: calling a Go engine or pipeline function that may record partial failures in a result struct rather than surfacing them as a returned Go error
content: After calling any engine or pipeline function that returns both a Go error and a result struct, always check `err` AND `result.ExitCode()`/`result.Errors` before emitting a success message or returning zero; never gate the success path on the Go error alone.
causal_note: Partial-failure pipeline functions routinely return a nil Go error while recording planning, fetch, or render failures inside the result struct; checking only `err` causes exit-0 with errors silently omitted — e.g. an invalid repo URL prints 'All skills are up to date.' instead of failing.

use_when: a pre-commit lint hook fails with 'no such file or directory', 'parallel golangci-lint is running', or a machine-wide lock error while multiple worktrees are active
content: When a golangci-lint pre-commit failure shows 'no such file or directory' (stale cross-worktree cache), run `golangci-lint cache clean` and retry; when it shows a lock-contention error (concurrent worktrees racing on /tmp/golangci-lint.lock), stash the change and wait for the concurrent lint load to drop before retrying — never bypass with --no-verify, as neither failure reflects a real code defect.
causal_note: golangci-lint shares a cache and a machine-wide lock across all worktrees. ob-3234e7a5: a stale cache held references to files only present in a sibling worktree, producing 'no such file or directory' errors on valid code. ob-e377f2b5: 15 concurrent worktrees serialized on the global lock, causing a status-flip commit to lose the race entirely and leaving stray uncommitted edits.

use_when: creating test fixtures under a testdata/ directory, adding Go integration test data files, or setting up any fixture files for automated tests
content: After creating any file under a `testdata/` directory, immediately run `git check-ignore -v <path>` to confirm it is not excluded. If it is, add an explicit `!<module>/testdata/` un-ignore entry to `.gitignore` before committing any test that depends on those fixtures.
causal_note: The repo's default `**/testdata/` gitignore rule causes `git add` to silently stage nothing with no error message — fixtures exist locally (local tests pass) but are never committed, producing CI failures with 'no such file or directory' on every clean checkout.
